title: Blog 1
content:
Amazon S3 Vectors now generally available with increased scale and performance Item Detail Original post Amazon S3 Vectors now generally available with increased scale and performance Source AWS News Blog Topic New service · Storage for AI Translated on [dd/mm/2026] Summary The post introduces Amazon S3 Vectors, a new bucket type that stores and queries vectors directly in S3, billed by storage and queries. S3 Vectors can serve as the vector store for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases: the Knowledge Base reads documents from a regular S3 bucket, chunks them, creates vectors and stores them in S3 Vectors.
Relevance to StudyMate This is why StudyMate uses S3 Vectors instead of OpenSearch Serverless: for a student project’s small data volume the cost is close to zero, whereas OpenSearch Serverless has a minimum hourly charge.

title: Create the Function
content:
Step 1: Create the function Open the AWS Lambda console → Create function. Choose Author from scratch. Function name: studymate-ask. Runtime: Python 3.12. Leave Execution role as Create a new role with basic Lambda permissions → Create function. 📷 Insert screenshot: Create function form → static/images/5-Workshop/5.5/01-create-function.png
Step 2: Paste the code In the Code tab, replace the content of lambda_function.py with the code below, then click Deploy.
import json import os import boto3 client = boto3.client("bedrock-agent-runtime") KB_ID = os.environ["KB_ID"] MODEL_ARN = os.environ["MODEL_ARN"] HEADERS = { "Content-Type": "application/json", "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*", } def reply(status, payload): return {"statusCode": status, "headers": HEADERS, "body": json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)} def lambda_handler(event, context): try: body = json.loads(event.get("body") or "{}") except json.JSONDecodeError: return reply(400, {"error": "Body must be JSON"}) question = (body.get("question") or "").strip() if not question or len(question) > 500: return reply(400, {"error": "Question must be 1-500 characters"}) resp = client.retrieve_and_generate( input={"text": question}, retrieveAndGenerateConfiguration={ "type": "KNOWLEDGE_BASE", "knowledgeBaseConfiguration": { "knowledgeBaseId": KB_ID, "modelArn": MODEL_ARN, }, }, ) sources = [] for citation in resp.get("citations", []): for ref in citation.get("retrievedReferences", []): uri = ref.get("location", {}).get("s3Location", {}).get("uri") if uri and uri not in sources: sources.append(uri) return reply(200, {"answer": resp["output"]["text"], "sources": sources}) What the code does Part Explanation boto3.client("bedrock-agent-runtime") Creates a client for calling the Knowledge Base. boto3 is the AWS SDK for Python and is already included in Lambda. os.environ["KB_ID"], os.environ["MODEL_ARN"] Reads settings from environment variables so they are not hard-coded. HEADERS Returns JSON and allows the browser to read the response (CORS). json.loads(event.get("body")) API Gateway passes the request body as a string; this converts it to a dictionary. Question length check Rejects empty or very long questions to limit abuse and cost. retrieve_and_generate(...) One call that both retrieves relevant chunks and has Nova Lite write the answer. citations loop Collects the S3 paths of the source files, without duplicates. reply(200, ...) Returns the answer and sources as JSON. ensure_ascii=False keeps Vietnamese characters readable. Step 3: Increase the timeout Lambda stops a function after 3 seconds by default, but the AI needs several seconds to write.
Configuration tab → General configuration → Edit. Timeout: 0 min 30 sec → Save. Step 4: Add environment variables Configuration → Environment variables → Edit → Add environment variable. Add the two variables below → Save. Key Value KB_ID Your Knowledge Base ID from section 5.4.1 MODEL_ARN arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1::foundation-model/amazon.nova-lite-v1:0 📷 Insert screenshot: environment variables KB_ID and MODEL_ARN → static/images/5-Workshop/5.5/02-env-vars.png
An ARN (Amazon Resource Name) is the full unique address of a resource on AWS. MODEL_ARN tells the code exactly which model to use.

title: Create the Knowledge Base
content:
Step 1: Start the wizard Open the Amazon Bedrock console. In the left menu, choose Knowledge Bases → Create → Knowledge Base with vector store. 📷 Insert screenshot: Create menu with Knowledge Base with vector store → static/images/5-Workshop/5.4/01-create-menu.png
Step 2: Knowledge Base details Knowledge Base name: studymate-kb. IAM permissions: Create and use a new service role. Bedrock creates a role that can read your bucket and call the embedding model. Data source: Amazon S3. Click Next. Step 3: Configure the data source S3 URI: click Browse S3 and choose studymate-docs-<your-name>. Parsing strategy and Chunking strategy: keep Default. Click Next. 📷 Insert screenshot: data source with the S3 URI selected → static/images/5-Workshop/5.4/02-data-source.png
Step 4: Embeddings model and vector store Embeddings model: Titan Text Embeddings V2. Vector store: Quick create a new vector store → Amazon S3 Vectors. Click Next, review, then Create Knowledge Base. Creation takes a few minutes. 📷 Insert screenshot: embeddings model and S3 Vectors selection → static/images/5-Workshop/5.4/03-vector-store.png
Do not choose Amazon OpenSearch Serverless. It charges a minimum hourly capacity even when idle, which can reach hundreds of USD per month.

title: Worklog
content:
Worklog This section records my 12-week internship. The first five weeks covered core AWS services (IAM, VPC, EC2, S3, RDS, DynamoDB, Lambda, API Gateway). From week 6 I worked on my project, StudyMate, a Q&A chatbot for the student handbook built with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway and Amazon S3.
Week 1: Program onboarding and securing the AWS account
Week 2: Networking and compute: Amazon VPC, Amazon EC2
Week 3: Storage: Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudFront
Week 4: Databases: Amazon RDS and Amazon DynamoDB
Week 5: Serverless: AWS Lambda and Amazon API Gateway
Week 6: Generative AI with Amazon Bedrock; choosing the project
Week 7: Building the Bedrock Knowledge Base
Week 8: Backend: a Lambda function calling Bedrock
Week 9: API Gateway and web frontend
Week 10: Security, monitoring and quality evaluation
Week 11: Writing the workshop and publishing the report on GitHub Pages
Week 12: Internship wrap-up

title: Workshop Overview
content:
How StudyMate works Think of StudyMate as a help desk at the university library. Each AWS service plays one role:
Library role AWS service What it does The desk where students ask Amazon S3 (static website) Serves the chat web page The intake window Amazon API Gateway Gives the page an HTTPS address to send questions to The desk clerk AWS Lambda Receives the question, asks the librarian, returns the answer The librarian Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base Finds the right pages in the documents The writer Amazon Nova Lite Reads those pages and writes a short answer The bookshelf Amazon S3 (private bucket) Stores the source PDFs The card catalogue Amazon S3 Vectors Stores the “meaning” of each passage so it can be found quickly Key concepts RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) Asking an AI model directly about your university’s rules does not work: it has never read them and may invent an answer. RAG adds a step: retrieve the relevant passages first, then let the model generate an answer using only those passages.
Chunking The Knowledge Base splits each PDF into small pieces (chunks) of a few paragraphs, so it can return just the relevant part instead of a whole 50-page file.
Embedding An embedding model (here Titan Text Embeddings V2) turns each chunk into a list of numbers (a vector). Passages with similar meaning get similar vectors, even if they use different words. “Scholarship” and “financial support for top students” end up close together.
Vector store A database built to store vectors and find the nearest ones fast. When a question arrives, it is also turned into a vector, and the vector store returns the closest chunks. This workshop uses Amazon S3 Vectors because it costs almost nothing at small scale.
IAM role An IAM user gives permissions to a person; an IAM role gives permissions to a service. The Lambda function gets a role that lets it call only the Knowledge Base and the model it needs.
What you will build A private S3 bucket holding the PDFs. A Bedrock Knowledge Base that indexes the PDFs into S3 Vectors. A Lambda function that calls the Knowledge Base. An HTTP API in API Gateway that exposes the Lambda function. A public S3 bucket hosting the chat page. Work step by step and test each part before moving on: Knowledge Base test in the console → Lambda test event → curl against the API → the web page. When something breaks, you will know exactly which step caused it.

title: Configure CORS and Test
content:
What is CORS? Browsers have a safety rule: a page served from address A may not call address B unless B explicitly allows it. The web page lives on S3 and the API lives on API Gateway, which are different addresses, so you must enable CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) on the API.
Configure CORS In studymate-api, choose CORS in the left menu → Configure. Fill in: Field Value Access-Control-Allow-Origin * Access-Control-Allow-Methods POST Access-Control-Allow-Headers content-type Save. 📷 Insert screenshot: CORS configuration → static/images/5-Workshop/5.6/03-cors.png
* allows any website to call the API, which is fine for a demo. In production, replace it with your website’s address.
Test with curl Run this in a terminal (replace the URL). This tests the API without the web page, so if it fails you know the problem is in the API or Lambda, not the page.
curl -X POST "https://abc123.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/ask" \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ -d '{"question": "Thủ tục bảo lưu kết quả học tập như thế nào?"}' Expected output:
{"answer": "...", "sources": ["s3://studymate-docs-.../quy-che-dao-tao.pdf"]} Add throttling (optional) To prevent abuse, open Throttling in the left menu → select the $default stage → Edit and set, for example, a rate limit of 5 and a burst limit of 10 requests.

title: Grant IAM Permissions
content:
Why this step is needed By default the Lambda role can only write logs to CloudWatch. It is not allowed to call Bedrock. You add an inline policy that grants exactly two permissions: query your Knowledge Base, and invoke Nova Lite. Granting only what is needed is called least privilege.
Step 1: Open the role In the function, open Configuration → Permissions. Click the role name under Execution role (e.g. studymate-ask-role-xxxx). The IAM console opens. Step 2: Add an inline policy Add permissions → Create inline policy. Switch to the JSON tab and paste the policy below. Replace ACCOUNT_ID with your 12-digit account ID (top right menu of the console) and KB_ID with your Knowledge Base ID. Next → Policy name: studymate-bedrock-access → Create policy. { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "QueryKnowledgeBase", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["bedrock:RetrieveAndGenerate", "bedrock:Retrieve"], "Resource": "arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:ACCOUNT_ID:knowledge-base/KB_ID" }, { "Sid": "InvokeNovaLite", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["bedrock:InvokeModel"], "Resource": "arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1::foundation-model/amazon.nova-lite-v1:0" } ] } Statement Meaning QueryKnowledgeBase Allows querying only the studymate-kb Knowledge Base InvokeNovaLite Allows invoking only the Nova Lite model 📷 Insert screenshot: inline policy in the JSON editor → static/images/5-Workshop/5.5/03-inline-policy.png
Step 3: Test the function Back in Lambda, open the Test tab → Create new event. Event name: ask-scholarship. Paste this event JSON: { "body": "{\"question\": \"Điều kiện để được xét học bổng là gì?\"}" } Click Test. The result should show "statusCode": 200 and a body containing answer and sources. 📷 Insert screenshot: successful test result with statusCode 200 → static/images/5-Workshop/5.5/04-test-result.png
AccessDeniedException means the policy is wrong: check ACCOUNT_ID, KB_ID and that you are in us-east-1. “Task timed out after 3.00 seconds” means you skipped the timeout step.

content:
1. AWS account and IAM user You need an AWS account and an IAM user with administrator permissions for this lab. Do not use the root user for daily work.
2. Select the region At the top right of the console, select US East (N. Virginia) us-east-1 and keep it for the whole workshop.
A region is a group of AWS data centers in one area. Resources created in one region do not show up in another. If you ever “lose” a resource, check the region first.
📷 Insert screenshot: region selector set to us-east-1 → static/images/5-Workshop/5.2/01-region.png
3. Create a cost alert Open Billing and Cost Management → Budgets → Create budget. Choose Use a template → Monthly cost budget. Budget amount: 5 USD. Enter your email address. Click Create budget. 📷 Insert screenshot: the created budget → static/images/5-Workshop/5.2/02-budget.png
4. Prepare the documents Prepare 2–3 text-based PDFs, for example your university’s student handbook and academic regulations.
Quick check: open the PDF and try to select a line of text. If you cannot, it is a scanned image and the Knowledge Base will not be able to read it.
5. Bedrock model access Serverless models on Amazon Bedrock are now enabled by default; there is no “Model access” page to visit. Anthropic (Claude) models still require a one-time use-case form, but this workshop uses Amazon Nova Lite, so you can skip that.

title: Proposal
content:
StudyMate A Student Handbook Q&A Chatbot on AWS 1. Executive Summary StudyMate is a chat web page that helps students look up academic regulations, the student handbook and administrative rules in Vietnamese. It uses RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation): it first retrieves relevant document passages, then has a language model write a short answer that cites the source file. The whole system is serverless on AWS, so there are no servers to manage, and the demo costs an estimated less than 1 USD per month.
2. Problem Statement Current Problem Regulations and the student handbook run to dozens of pages spread across several PDFs. Students struggle to find specific information (scholarship conditions, conduct scoring, leave of absence…). Repeated questions pile up at the academic office and with academic advisors. Solution Load all documents into an Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base. Students ask questions in natural language on a web page. The system answers only from the university’s documents and always shows sources so students can verify. Benefits Fast, always-available lookups for students. Fewer repeated questions for the academic office. Easy updates: upload a new file to S3 and click Sync. Very low cost thanks to the serverless design and S3 Vectors. 3. Solution Architecture Solution Architecture Question flow (1–6): (1) The student loads the static web page from Amazon S3 → (2) the page sends the question to Amazon API Gateway (POST /ask) → (3) API Gateway invokes AWS Lambda → (4) Lambda calls the retrieve_and_generate API of the Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base → (5a) the Knowledge Base uses Titan Text Embeddings V2 to turn the question into a vector, (5b) then finds the 5 nearest chunks in Amazon S3 Vectors → (6) Amazon Nova Lite writes the answer with sources. The result returns through Lambda and API Gateway to the browser.
Ingestion flow (A–D): (A) The administrator uploads PDFs to a private S3 bucket → (B) on Sync, the Knowledge Base reads and chunks them → (C) Titan Text Embeddings V2 turns each chunk into a vector → (D) the vectors are stored in Amazon S3 Vectors.
Monitoring and security: Lambda writes logs to Amazon CloudWatch. Two IAM roles (one for Lambda, one for the Knowledge Base) grant only the permissions each needs.
AWS Services Used Service Role Amazon S3 Stores source PDFs; hosts the static web UI Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases Chunks documents, creates embeddings, retrieves and generates answers Amazon S3 Vectors Low-cost vector store for the Knowledge Base Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 Converts text into vectors Amazon Nova Lite Language model that writes answers AWS Lambda Receives the question, calls Bedrock, returns JSON Amazon API Gateway Provides an HTTPS endpoint for the web page Amazon CloudWatch Logs, error and duration monitoring AWS IAM Least-privilege permissions for each service AWS Budgets Cost alerts Component Design Frontend A single plain index.html (HTML, CSS, JavaScript), no framework. Hosted with S3 static website hosting. Backend A Python 3.12 Lambda function of about 40 lines. Calls Bedrock’s retrieve_and_generate API: one call both retrieves passages and generates the answer. Validates input (question of 1–500 characters). Data Source documents: 2–3 text-based PDFs. Vectors stored in S3 Vectors, created and managed by the Knowledge Base. Security The documents bucket stays private; only the web bucket is publicly readable. Lambda may only call the specific Knowledge Base and model it needs. API Gateway throttling limits request rates. 4. Technical Implementation Implementation Phases Prepare the account, region and cost alerts. Upload documents to S3; create and test the Knowledge Base. Write the Lambda function; configure IAM. Create the API Gateway; configure CORS. Write and host the web UI. Test, monitor, clean up. Technical Requirements Programming Languages Python 3.12 (Lambda) HTML, CSS, JavaScript (UI) Libraries boto3 (included in the Lambda runtime) Tools AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, Visual Studio Code, Git, Hugo 5. Timeline & Milestones Week Work 1–5 AWS fundamentals: IAM, VPC, EC2, S3, RDS, DynamoDB, Lambda, API Gateway 6 Explore Bedrock and RAG; write the proposal 7 Build the Knowledge Base 8 Write the Lambda function and IAM policy 9 API Gateway and web UI 10 Security, monitoring, quality evaluation 11 Write the workshop; publish the report on GitHub Pages 12 Demo, cleanup, wrap-up 6. Budget Estimation Infrastructure Cost Estimate Assumptions: us-east-1; 3 PDFs (about 50,000 tokens); 1,000 questions/month, each about 3,000 input and 300 output tokens.
Item Estimated cost (USD/month) Amazon S3 (documents + website, under 1 GB) ~0.03 Amazon S3 Vectors (storage + queries) < 0.01 Titan Text Embeddings V2 < 0.01 Amazon Nova Lite (3M input, 0.3M output tokens) ~0.25 AWS Lambda, API Gateway, CloudWatch (within Free Tier) ~0.00 Total < 1.00 These are estimates based on list prices, which can change. [Insert your AWS Pricing Calculator link here]
Cost Control Guidelines Create a 5 USD AWS Budget from day one. Do not pick Amazon OpenSearch Serverless as the vector store: it bills a minimum hourly capacity even when idle, which can reach hundreds of USD per month. Delete all resources after the demo (section 5.9). 7. Risk Assessment Risk Matrix Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation Model answers wrongly or invents facts Medium High Answer only from documents; always show sources Unexpected charges Low Medium AWS Budgets; clean up after the demo API abuse Low Medium API Gateway throttling; question length limit Scanned PDFs without text Medium Medium Use text-based PDFs or enable advanced parsing 8. Expected Outcomes Technical Outcomes A working chat page that answers within a few seconds and cites sources. At least 16 of 20 test questions answered correctly. A workshop that rebuilds the whole system from scratch. Practical Value Can be extended into an academic assistant for the whole university. A foundation for the AI assistant in student-management projects.

title: Sync and Test
content:
Sync the data source Creating the Knowledge Base does not read the documents yet. You must run a Sync.
On the studymate-kb page, scroll to Data source. Select the data source → Sync. Wait until the sync status shows it has completed. 📷 Insert screenshot: data source with sync completed → static/images/5-Workshop/5.4/04-sync.png
Whenever you add or change a PDF in the bucket, run Sync again. That is all it takes to update StudyMate’s knowledge.
Test in the console Click Test Knowledge Base on the right side of the page. Click Select model → Amazon → Nova Lite → Apply. Ask a question whose answer is in your documents, e.g. “What are the conditions for a scholarship?” The answer should include citation numbers; click one to see the source passage. 📷 Insert screenshot: test panel with an answer and its citation → static/images/5-Workshop/5.4/05-test.png
If this test works, the hardest part is done. The remaining sections only expose this capability through a web page.

title: Upload Documents to S3
content:
What is Amazon S3? Amazon S3 is AWS’s online storage, similar to Google Drive. A bucket is a top-level folder; each file inside is an object. This bucket stays private because only the Knowledge Base needs to read it.
Create the bucket Open the Amazon S3 console → Create bucket. Bucket type: General purpose. Bucket name: studymate-docs-<your-name> (bucket names must be unique across all AWS accounts, so add your name). Keep Block all public access checked. Leave the other settings as default → Create bucket. 📷 Insert screenshot: Create bucket form → static/images/5-Workshop/5.3/01-create-bucket.png
Upload the PDFs Open the new bucket → Upload. Drag in your PDFs → Upload. 📷 Insert screenshot: object list showing the uploaded PDFs → static/images/5-Workshop/5.3/02-objects.png
Use clear file names such as quy-che-dao-tao.pdf. The chatbot shows the file name as its source, so readable names make answers easier to trust.

title: Create the Knowledge Base
content:
What the Knowledge Base does This is the core of StudyMate, but AWS does most of the work. When you click Sync, the Knowledge Base:
Reads the PDFs from your S3 bucket. Splits them into chunks. Calls Titan Text Embeddings V2 to turn each chunk into a vector. Stores the vectors in Amazon S3 Vectors. When a question arrives, it is turned into a vector too, and the Knowledge Base returns the closest chunks.

title: Create the Lambda Function
content:
What is AWS Lambda? Lambda runs your code without a server you manage. The code runs only when something calls it, then stops, and you pay only for that run time. StudyMate’s Lambda function is the “desk clerk”: it receives a question, asks the Knowledge Base, and returns the answer.
Content Create the function Grant IAM permissions

title: Workshop
content:
Building StudyMate: a Student Handbook Q&A Chatbot with Amazon Bedrock Overview In this workshop you build StudyMate from scratch in the AWS Management Console. Students type a question on a web page; the system finds the relevant passages in the university’s PDFs and has an AI model write a short answer with the source file.
You only write two small files: a ~40-line Python Lambda function and one HTML page. Everything else is console configuration.
Time About 2 hours Level Beginner (you only need an AWS account and an IAM user) Cost Under 1 USD if you clean up afterwards Region US East (N. Virginia) us-east-1 Content Workshop overview Prerequisites Upload documents to Amazon S3 Create the Bedrock Knowledge Base Create the Lambda function Create the API with API Gateway Host the web frontend on S3 Testing and monitoring Clean up resources

title: Create the API with API Gateway
content:
Why API Gateway? A Lambda function has no web address of its own. Amazon API Gateway gives it a public HTTPS URL so the web page can send questions to it. POST /ask means “send data to the /ask path”.
Content Create the HTTP API Configure CORS and test

title: Self-evaluation
content:
When I joined the First Cloud AI Journey (FCAJ) program, I knew very little about AWS: I had only created an account, a database and an IAM user. After 12 weeks I had built a serverless application on my own using Amazon Bedrock, AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudWatch, and turned it into a workshop others can follow.
Beyond technical knowledge, I built the habits of reading AWS documentation in English, reading logs to find errors, and always cleaning up resources to control cost.

title: Host the Web Frontend on S3
content:
Overview The web page is a single index.html with an input box, a Send button and a little JavaScript that calls the API. S3 can serve static websites: put the file in a bucket, enable website hosting, and allow public read access.
This is a second bucket. The documents bucket from 5.3 stays private; only this website bucket is public.
Step 1: Create the website bucket S3 → Create bucket → name studymate-web-<your-name>. Uncheck Block all public access and tick the acknowledgement box. Create bucket. Step 2: Enable static website hosting Open the bucket → Properties tab → scroll to Static website hosting → Edit. Enable, Index document: index.html → Save changes. Step 3: Add the bucket policy Permissions tab → Bucket policy → Edit → paste the policy (replace the bucket name) → Save changes.
{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "PublicReadForWebsite", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": "*", "Action": "s3:GetObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::studymate-web-YOURNAME/*" } ] } Step 4: Create and upload index.html Create index.html on your computer with the content below. Replace API_URL with your Invoke URL followed by /ask.
<!doctype html> <html lang="vi"> <head> <meta charset="utf-8"> <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> <title>StudyMate</title> <style> body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; max-width: 680px; margin: 40px auto; padding: 0 16px; } #log div { margin: 12px 0; padding: 10px 14px; border-radius: 10px; } .q { background: #e2f1ed; } .a { background: #f3f4f4; white-space: pre-wrap; } .src { font-size: 12px; color: #667; margin-top: 6px; } form { display: flex; gap: 8px; } input { flex: 1; padding: 10px; } </style> </head> <body> <h1>StudyMate</h1> <p>Hỏi về quy chế đào tạo và sổ tay sinh viên.</p> <div id="log"></div> <form id="f"> <input id="q" placeholder="Ví dụ: Điều kiện xét học bổng?" required maxlength="500"> <button>Gửi</button> </form> <script> const API_URL = "https://xxxx.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/ask"; // thay bằng Invoke URL + /ask const log = document.getElementById("log"); function add(cls, text) { const d = document.createElement("div"); d.className = cls; d.textContent = text; log.appendChild(d); return d; } document.getElementById("f").addEventListener("submit", async (e) => { e.preventDefault(); const input = document.getElementById("q"); const question = input.value.trim(); input.value = ""; add("q", question); const box = add("a", "Đang tìm câu trả lời..."); try { const res = await fetch(API_URL, { method: "POST", headers: { "content-type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ question }) }); const data = await res.json(); box.textContent = data.answer || data.error; if (data.sources && data.sources.length) { const s = document.createElement("div"); s.className = "src"; s.textContent = "Nguồn: " + data.sources.map(u => u.split("/").pop()).join(", "); box.appendChild(s); } } catch (err) { box.textContent = "Không gọi được API: " + err.message; } }); </script> </body> </html> Upload index.html to the bucket. Then go to Properties → Static website hosting and open the Bucket website endpoint.
📷 Insert screenshot: StudyMate page answering a question with sources → static/images/5-Workshop/5.7/01-website.png
The S3 website endpoint uses plain HTTP. As an extension, put Amazon CloudFront in front of the bucket to get HTTPS and keep the bucket private.

title: Testing and Monitoring
content:
Answer quality test Write 20 questions whose answers you know are in the documents. Ask each one on the web page and record the result in a table like this: # Question Correct? Cited source 1 What are the scholarship conditions? ✅ quy-che-dao-tao.pdf 2 … Ask 2–3 questions outside the documents (e.g. “What’s the weather today?”) to check that the system does not invent answers. Result: [x/20 correct]
Monitoring with CloudWatch Open CloudWatch → Log groups → /aws/lambda/studymate-ask. Open the latest log stream. Each request logs its Duration and any errors. In the Lambda console, the Monitor tab shows invocation count, duration and error charts. 📷 Insert screenshot: Lambda Monitor tab charts → static/images/5-Workshop/5.8/01-monitor.png
Common errors Error Cause Fix AccessDeniedException The Lambda role lacks permissions Check ACCOUNT_ID, KB_ID and region in the policy (5.5.2) Task timed out after 3.00 seconds Default timeout Raise the timeout to 30 seconds (5.5.1) CORS error in the browser console CORS not configured Configure CORS on the API (5.6.2) “Sorry, I am unable to assist…” for every question Data not synced, or scanned PDFs Run Sync (5.4.2); use text-based PDFs {"message":"Not Found"} Wrong URL Make sure the URL ends with /ask

title: Clean Up Resources
content:
Delete resources in this order so nothing keeps charging you.
1. API Gateway API Gateway → select studymate-api → Delete.
2. Lambda and logs Lambda → select studymate-ask → Actions → Delete. CloudWatch → Log groups → select /aws/lambda/studymate-ask → Actions → Delete log group(s). 3. Knowledge Base Amazon Bedrock → Knowledge Bases → select studymate-kb → Delete. Type the confirmation text and confirm.
4. S3 Vectors Amazon S3 → Vector buckets → open the vector bucket created by Bedrock → delete its index, then delete the vector bucket.
5. S3 buckets For both studymate-docs-<your-name> and studymate-web-<your-name>: select the bucket → Empty → confirm → then Delete → confirm.
6. IAM roles IAM → Roles → delete the roles created during the workshop:
AmazonBedrockExecutionRoleForKnowledgeBase_... studymate-ask-role-... 7. Check billing A day later, open Billing and Cost Management → Bills to confirm no charges are still accruing.
